etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French appréciation. Morphologically appreciate +‎ -ion

definitions.definition: A fair valuation or estimate of merit, worth, weight, etc.; recognition of excellence; gratitude and esteem.

quote.citation: 2014 September 16, Ian Jack, “Is this the end of Britishness”, in The Guardian:
quote.text: The English, until relatively recently, seem to have imagined “English” and “British” to be interchangeable, as if Britain was just a bigger England. Our dualism gave us a better appreciation of the nation-state we lived in, though if Britain was a “nation” as well as a “state”, where did that leave Scotland?

quote.citation: 1874, John Richard Green, History of the English People, Volume I:
quote.text: His foreboding showed his appreciation of Henry's character.
